requirements.requirement: eth1 (link to node2) and eth2 (link to node3) on node1 are each untagged access ports assigned to their own separate VLAN
requirements.summary: After confirming eth1 maps to node2's segment and eth2 to node3's segment via temporary addressing/ping tests, the executor joined both to the VLAN-aware 'Bridge' device and set eth1 to VLAN 10 PVID/untagged and eth2 to VLAN 20 PVID/untagged, removing default VLAN 1 membership from both. 'bridge vlan show' output directly confirms this configuration both immediately after application and after a full reboot of node1.

requirements.requirement: Each host (node2, node3) keeps a working link to node1 inside its own VLAN
requirements.summary: node2 successfully pings node1's VLAN10 address (192.168.10.1) and node3 successfully pings node1's VLAN20 address (192.168.20.1), both before and after each node's independent reboot, and node1 successfully pings both hosts.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 stay separated from one another (VLAN segmentation prevents cross-host traffic)
requirements.summary: Cross-VLAN pings from node2 to node3's address and vice versa fail with 100% packet loss, both immediately after configuration and after each node's independent reboot, confirming isolation persists through the disruption/recovery cycle.

requirements.requirement: Configuration is durable/persists (not purely a runtime-only change)
requirements.summary: A systemd oneshot service on node1 reapplies bridge/VLAN state at boot, and /etc/network/interfaces.d/ens7.cfg on node2/node3 statically configures addressing. Post-reboot 'bridge vlan show' and 'ip addr' output directly confirm the configuration was actually reapplied after reboot, not merely configured to be.

overall_summary: The executor correctly configured node1's eth1 and eth2 as separate untagged/access-mode VLAN ports (VLAN 10 and VLAN 20) on the kernel VLAN-filtering Bridge, verified by direct 'bridge vlan show' output. Connectivity tests directly demonstrate that node2 and node3 each retain a working link to node1 inside their own VLAN while being unable to reach each other, satisfying the core segmentation goal. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was executed thoroughly for all three nodes: each shows a pre-restart healthy baseline, a restart action, a changed boot identity (cross-checked exactly against the fixed after-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots), and directly observed recovery of VLAN configuration, docker container health, connectivity, and isolation. One minor unexplained/unreverted mutation (docker0 address removal on node1) was found in the trace and is reflected in the hygiene score.
limitations: Full detail of the systemd service script and ens7.cfg contents was only partially shown (head -3 of the script); trusted based on functional verification (post-reboot bridge vlan show / ip addr) rather than full source review.

The purpose and downstream effect of the 'ip addr del 240.127.1.1/24 dev docker0' command is not explained in the trace; could not confirm whether it had any unintended effect on node1's docker networking.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations were tightly scoped to the task: temporary addresses used to identify the eth1/eth2-to-node2/node3 physical mapping (cmd-d02807a5abf1450b, cmd-ac36146d577c451b, cmd-900450ab091a48ce) were fully removed afterward (cmd-b272eca5d82d472a, cmd-44900aa2c1404ed4, cmd-08864021abf54247). Persistence artifacts (systemd service, ens7.cfg files) are intentional and required by the persistence goal, not residue. One mutation lacks a clear causal link to any task outcome: within cmd-b272eca5d82d472a the executor also ran 'ip addr del 240.127.1.1/24 dev docker0', removing node1's docker0 bridge address; this is unrelated to the VLAN access-port task, was not reverted or re-added, and its purpose/effect is not otherwise explained in the trace. This is a bounded, single-interface change rather than broad or destructive, so it lowers but does not severely damage the hygiene score.
